ecommerce_order_pipeline.description: Automated order processing — from purchase to fulfillment notification
ecommerce_order_pipeline.example: Customer places Shopify order -> Stripe confirms payment -> Klaviyo sends confirmation email -> Slack notifies fulfillment team -> Supabase logs analytics
ecommerce_order_pipeline.business_value: Eliminates manual order monitoring. Team gets instant alerts. Customers get immediate confirmation. Analytics capture every touchpoint.

client_onboarding.description: Automated new client setup across CRM, documents, and project management
client_onboarding.example: New deal closes in HubSpot -> Google Drive creates client folder from template -> Slack creates client channel -> QuickBooks creates customer record -> Google Calendar schedules kickoff meeting
client_onboarding.business_value: Standardizes onboarding for every client. No dropped steps. Time to first meeting reduced from days to minutes.

patient_recall_system.description: Automated patient follow-up for overdue checkups and treatment plans
patient_recall_system.example: Supabase query finds patients overdue for cleaning -> Twilio sends SMS reminder -> Google Calendar offers booking slots -> HubSpot logs interaction -> QuickBooks prepares estimated invoice
patient_recall_system.business_value: Keeps chairs full without manual phone campaigns. 30-40% higher recall rates. Reduces front-desk workload by 5+ hours/week.

competitive_intelligence.description: Automated competitor monitoring and market research
competitive_intelligence.example: Brave Search finds competitor updates -> Playwright scrapes pricing pages -> Supabase stores historical data -> Slack alerts team of changes -> Notion updates competitive analysis doc
competitive_intelligence.business_value: Never miss a competitor price change or feature launch. Build historical pricing database. React faster to market shifts.

financial_reporting.description: Cross-platform financial overview pulling from payments, accounting, and analytics
financial_reporting.example: Stripe provides revenue data -> QuickBooks adds expense context -> Google Analytics shows acquisition costs -> Supabase aggregates into unified dashboard -> Slack delivers weekly summary
financial_reporting.business_value: Single source of truth for business health. Automated weekly reports replace manual spreadsheet work. Faster decision-making.

content_to_campaign.description: Content creation pipeline from research to published marketing campaign
content_to_campaign.example: Brave Search researches trending topics -> Google Drive stores drafts -> AI generates email copy -> Mailchimp/Klaviyo creates segmented campaign -> Google Analytics tracks performance
content_to_campaign.business_value: Reduces campaign creation from days to hours. Research-backed content. Automated performance tracking closes the feedback loop.

getting_started.description: Practical guidance for businesses adopting MCP servers
steps: Start with 2-3 servers that connect your most-used daily tools
Prioritize read-only servers first to reduce risk (most servers default to read-only)
Add write capabilities only after validating data quality and accuracy
Build one integration pattern end-to-end before adding more servers
Monitor token usage — each MCP server call consumes API tokens
common_mistakes: Connecting too many servers at once — start small, validate, then expand
Skipping authentication setup — always use environment variables for API keys, never hardcode
Ignoring rate limits — most APIs have usage caps that MCP servers must respect
Using write operations on production data before testing on staging/sandbox
Not setting up read-only mode for databases — always use read_only=true when exploring production data
